explanation: Purcell shows that Aztec ethics judged actions by how well they fit a person's social role and served the community, which is the opposite of judging actions 'irrespective of the context.' So the Aztecs would have rejected the idea that morality can be measured by standards independent of a person's social circumstances. Choice B shifts the focus to who does the judging (outsiders), which the text never discusses, and C wrongly assumes the Aztecs had behaviors regarded as good in all contexts.

For project leaders, the bar for providing medicinal plants is about 2, while the bar for improving the local microclimate is about 3, so leaders rated medicinal plants lower. Choice C reverses this relationship. Choices B and D mention educational opportunities and tourist attractions, which are not shown in the graph, and B also contradicts the project leaders' equal ratings.

The text asks what grounds opposition to lying if we don't have an absolute duty to tell the truth, and presents Pallikkathayil's answer: a duty to respect others' agency that requires truthfulness except in certain cases. Choice A captures this. Choice C is tempting but wrong, because her duty is explicitly not inviolable — it allows exceptions.

The claim is about sex differences in the response to neuron activation, so we need to compare each CNO group with its own saline group. CNO-treated females rose far above saline-treated females (peaking near 1,400 beam breaks), while CNO-treated males stayed only modestly above saline-treated males. Choice B compares two saline groups, so it says nothing about the response to CNO, and choices A and D misdescribe the graph.

Choice C shows John working from early morning until late afternoon, going from fountain to fountain, so bent from labor that he never straightens — clear signs of hard work and devotion to his job. Choice A describes him happily going home with his earnings, and D describes what he did with old jugs; neither shows dedicated work.

The researcher claims that controlled fear can improve mood and confidence. Feeling 'very accomplished' reflects increased confidence, and feeling 'less stressed' reflects a better mood, so A illustrates both parts. Choice D mentions relief but doesn't address confidence, and C describes becoming less scared rather than any benefit afterward.

The conclusion is about anatomy (head shape) affecting the ability to tell speech from nonspeech. Choice B compares long- and short-headed dogs on the difference between hearing real language and the scrambled nonspeech recording, which directly tests that. Choice D is tempting, but it compares two languages, which is about telling languages apart, not speech from nonspeech.

For pin flowers, every genus spent more time on damaged flowers than intact ones (e.g., Habropoda 2.7 to 5.4). For thrum flowers, damage increased time only for Habropoda (4.1 to 9.5) and Osmia (7.1 to 8.3) and decreased it for Pierid and Xylocopa, so the effect depended on both morph and genus. Choice C is wrong because Osmia actually spent more time on damaged thrum flowers, and D gives intact-flower data only.

The scientists say the known benefits of deep sleep are not enough to outweigh the danger it creates, yet sleep is still widespread. The logical implication is that deep sleep must have other benefits that haven't been discovered yet. Choice D is a general statement about benefits and risks that doesn't follow from the argument about the known benefits being insufficient.

The declaration was written in the language of international diplomacy, reassured neighboring nations and the United States, and addressed people in other colonies. All of this points to audiences beyond the Haitian people it was explicitly addressed to. The other choices raise ideas (models from other countries, French surprise, Haitian opposition) that the text gives no support for.

Choice C says that being shut up in the house with a sleepy aunt and no companions makes life dull and leaves one 'ready for any new sensation,' showing both the monotony of Odalie's life and her eagerness to escape it. Choice B describes her secluded home but not her desire to escape, and A shows her tired of Mardi Gras rather than eager for change.

The underlined claim is that the sculptures look delicate but are actually durable. Materials that are 'both flexible and strong' explain both the flowing appearance and the durability. The other choices describe design methods or local themes, not durability.

The text focuses on Flanagan's work as FTP director: she created jobs for over 12,500 theater workers and kept ticket prices low so many people could see theater for the first time. Choice D combines both accomplishments. Choices A, B, and C are supporting details, not the main idea.

The text explains that Farmer broadened the kinds of primary sources historians use and that this produced a better understanding of the movement and of Black women's roles in it. Choice A states this. Choice B is too extreme — the text says earlier histories focused on ideological works, not that they ignored intellectual dimensions.

The claim contrasts read-straight-through genres like fiction with flip-through nonfiction. In 2016, e-books were 10.5% of cookbook sales but 36.7% of science fiction and fantasy sales, which shows exactly that contrast. Choices B and D compare one genre to itself over time, and C compares two fiction genres.

Rail is competitive because it avoids the long lead times of air travel, but the model shows long lead times appear when trains approach capacity. Adding more trains would increase capacity and keep lead times short. Choice D describes giving up rail's advantage rather than preserving it, and C would add lead time.

The text says the map surprisingly showed a magnetic field with no clear pattern or direction, while researchers expected a uniform field like those in other galactic bones. So the surprise was that the field was not uniform. Choice C is the opposite of what happened, and the text says nothing about strength (A) or earlier mappings (B).

The text says Hunt uses broad forms rather than exact accuracy, and both examples (a strange, machine-like Arachne and stylized flames for Ida B. Wells) show subjects depicted unrealistically. Choice D is tempting, but the text doesn't say his style changed over time; both early and recent works are described as non-literal.

The problem with herbicides is that they also kill harmless plants. Engineered DNA that blocks E. esula reproduction would target only that species, reducing its numbers without harming other organisms. Choice A still relies on herbicides, and B and C don't follow from inhibiting reproduction.

In choice B, Richard says he hasn't yet shaken off his 'regal thoughts' and has hardly learned to 'flatter, bow, and bend my knee,' meaning he isn't ready to act subservient to the new king. Choice D also refers to the new king, but Richard there grudgingly says 'God save the King,' which is closer to submission; A and C focus on lost identity and grief.

The text says the cave's ceiling was only a few feet high, so there was no spot from which the ten-foot-wide glyphs could be seen or photographed whole. That is a problem with the cave's dimensions. Choice C is the opposite of what happened — the team did build a 3D model to solve the problem.
The table lists the southern stoplight loosejaw at 500–2,000 meters below the surface. Choice D (250–500) doesn't match any row, and the black seadevil's range (250–2,000) is a different species.

In 2017 the American Indian museum had 1.2 million visits, its highest, and the African American History and Culture museum had 2.4 million, also its highest. No other year is the peak for both museums. In 2019 the African American museum was high (2.0) but the American Indian museum was at its lowest.

The example must show a country that did not have rising revenue. South Korea's revenue dropped from $21.0 billion in 2016 to $17.2 billion in 2017, which breaks the trend. Choice B is false (Japan rose from $33.5 to $45.3 billion), and A refers to resident spending, which the table doesn't show.

Bonding trust (people known personally) stays around 96–97% in all three years, while bridging trust (people met for the first time) moves from about 46% to 55% to 53%. So bonding trust was steady and bridging trust varied more. Choice D is wrong because bonding trust did not decline, and C is wrong because bonding trust was always higher than bridging trust.

To show males and females share the same sponge, each sponge needs both sexes. The graph shows sponge 1 with 17 males and 13 females, sponge 2 with 1 male and 2 females, and sponge 3 with 2 males and 1 female. Choices B and D each mention only one sex, and A is false because sponge 1 has no undetermined sharks.

The crisis came from coins falling below the 80% silver level that traders accepted, so confidence would be restored by raising the silver content of coins back above 80%. Doing so would be costly, which explains the phrase 'despite Sidon's persistent oppressive financial obligations.' Choice C is tempting, but heavier coins with the same 74% silver would still look yellowish and still fall below the accepted standard.

The highest incorporated self-employment rate in the table is 8.9%, for management, business, and financial services. Construction (choice C) has the highest unincorporated rate (14.8%), but its incorporated rate is only 4.4%.

The team claims the whales may not survive only on stored energy during migration. Seeing the whales feed while migrating would show they take in new energy along the way. Choice A is about other animals feeding, not the whales, and C and D concern the number or timing of observations.

note: The last line of the poem excerpt ('And keep my drooping eyelids open wide,') was merged into the prompt field instead of the passage.
explanation: The tired speaker goes to bed, but then a 'journey in my head' begins as his thoughts travel to the friend and keep his 'drooping eyelids open wide.' So he is thinking about the friend instead of falling asleep. Choice A is tempting, but the speaker is awake, not dreaming, and the journey is only in his thoughts, not a planned trip (B).

Choice A says poetry can fortify or demolish souls and give or take away faith and vigor, and that literature gives a people 'the desire and strength for life' — directly linking a society's spiritual well-being to its literature. Choice B is about literature recording history, and C discusses losing faith without connecting it to literature.

The LNH predicts that more non-native speakers (higher exotericity) means less grammatical complexity. Fusion and informativity are measures of complexity, so a positive correlation between each of them and exotericity would contradict the LNH, supporting the researchers' claim. Choice B describes a negative correlation between complexity and exotericity, which is what the LNH predicts, so it would support the LNH instead.

The narrator realizes Bill was 'desirous to avoid' seafaring men: he peeks at any seaman through the curtain before entering and stays silent around them. He asks about them so he won't run into one unexpectedly. Choice A is the family's first, mistaken guess that he wanted company.

The fungus spreads through the air from tree to nearby tree, and the surviving trees were in a hard-to-reach valley. It follows that their isolation kept them far enough from infected trees to escape the disease. The other choices don't explain how these particular trees avoided infection.

The researchers found that on rocky planets, NH3 likely can't reach detectable levels without life, so detecting it there would point to life. On mini-Neptunes, though, NH3 can form from high pressure and temperature alone, so it wouldn't indicate life. Choice A makes an unsupported comparison of likelihoods, and D contradicts the finding about rocky planets.

The exceptional moon orbits in the same direction as Saturn's spin, so its orbit is prograde. It is the one moon not thought to be a remnant of a broken-up body, and its eccentric orbit suggests a different origin. Choice C contradicts this by tying it to a collision, and A wrongly says it shares the others' origin.

In choice B, Amal hears the girl is gathering flowers — a chore — and says that's why her feet 'seem so glad' and her anklets jingle 'so merrily.' This shows him imagining that a worker is carefree. Choice D expresses Amal's own wish to go outside, not his view of others' work.

Poor lighting discourages new or inexperienced cyclists, so better lighting could remove that barrier and lead more of them to ride. Choice B is wrong because lighting has little effect on experienced cyclists, and A reverses the expected effect.

The text says Vargas altered classic songs by performing them much more slowly than other ranchera singers. Choice A describes the other singers, not Vargas, and B and C contradict the text, which says she did perform classic songs written from a male point of view.

The narrator describes how the earth disappears, the moon looks like another balloon, and the travelers stop speaking and thinking, floating in 'delicious inertia.' The group is fully absorbed in this new view of the world. Choice A is tempting because of 'alone in space,' but the whole group shares a joyful experience, not growing isolation, and nothing suggests they are troubled (C).

As the eclipse progresses, the light goes from bright to mid-range to low. The device plays a flute in bright light, a clarinet in mid-range light, and clicking in low light, so the sounds go flute, clarinet, clicking. Choices C and D describe changes in speed or volume, which the device isn't said to produce.

To be hot or warm Jupiters, all planets need a mass over 0.25 Jupiters, and the lowest mass in the table is 0.85. Four planets have orbital periods under 10 days, while TOI-1478 b has a period of 10.180 days, making it the one warm Jupiter. Choice B confuses TOI-1478 b's distance (153 parsecs) with its orbital period, and A wrongly says no planet's period exceeds 10 days.

Payload capacity is holding force divided by weight. The Ultra-Fast Robot Hand has more than four times the Yale Model T's holding force, and the graph shows it weighs only slightly more (about 505 g vs. 490 g), so its ratio — and payload capacity — must be higher. Choice A is true but doesn't compare the two weights, and C is about the Permanent Magnet Hand, not the comparison in the conclusion.

The hypothesis is that the sail helped Spinosaurus chase prey that make quick, evasive movements, which requires turning quickly. If the model with a sail completed sharp turns faster underwater, that would support the hypothesis. Choice D would weaken it by showing the sail slowed the animal, and B and C don't relate to chasing agile prey.

The sea stars chose the poor, starved urchins in 37.5% of trials — nearly as often as the rich ones (42.7%). This shows they don't avoid nutritionally poor urchins like those in barrens, so rebuilding their populations could help control barrens. Choice B contradicts the results, and A and C bring in other prey or other sea star species that weren't tested.

The narrator couldn't remember what Radha Aunty looked like, so he went to look at the family photographs to get an idea of her appearance. The other choices — a story, his father's clothes, or reminding his aunt of an event — aren't mentioned.

The text warns that today's beliefs may have been unfamiliar to Tanner and his contemporaries. Scholars who forget this could interpret the painting using modern values that don't fit its time — that is, judge it by historically inappropriate standards. The other choices introduce ideas (his contemporaries' views, his political activity, a critique of artists) the text doesn't raise.

Choice B pairs her pleasant appearance ('her lovely nose,' a little gold powder-box) with her unpleasant attitude (shaking the puff 'as though she loathed it'). Choices A, C, and D show her bad attitude but say nothing about her pleasant appearance, so they don't show the contrast.

The claim is that the film is largely imagined but informed by history. Choice D shows both parts: Powers found only superficial details about the meeting (so much of it is imagined) but read extensively about the four men to portray what might have happened (so it's informed). Choice C describes the story's themes without addressing its accuracy.

The text says handshakes build trust and the robot is meant to improve human-robot interactions. A realistic handshake would help people feel comfortable with the robot. Choice C is about how robots look, which isn't the focus, and B and D don't explain why realism matters.

Monkeys given physically hard tasks were judged by the same criteria as those given easy tasks, so a monkey might fail because of the dexterity required, not because of its intelligence. That means the results could show differences in cognitive ability that aren't really there. Choice B is tempting, but the flaw makes failures unreliable, so the results aren't especially good at identifying tasks beyond the monkeys' cognitive capacity.

The conclusion is that less crop variety may reduce total pollen collection. If honey from Kerinci (many crops) had much more pollen than honey from Kampar (one crop), that directly supports it. Choice A is about the variety of pollen sources, not the total amount, and B only compares two colonies at the same site.

The claim is that more informed voters are more likely to vote. At every point on the scale from 1 to 7, the high-information bar is taller than the low-information bar. Choice C is true of the graph but is about political orientation rather than information level, and D isn't shown by the graph at all.

In choice B the speaker says whoever brought the first wood and coal to start the fire 'did his part well,' which is direct praise for the fire's builder. Choice A describes people working without praising anyone, and C and D describe the fire dying and people going to bed.

If the ITCZ had simply shifted south, Central America would be dry while Peru was wet; if it expanded both north and south, both regions would get rain at the same time. So strongly correlated high rainfall at both caves (Yok Balum in Central America and Huagapo in Peru) would support expansion. Choice C describes the opposite pattern — dry in Central America while Peru was wet — which fits a simple southward shift.

To show that method affects the estimate, we need estimates from different methods that differ a lot. Meers used body-mass scaling and got 183,000–235,000 newtons, far beyond the other studies, while the two muscular and skeletal modeling studies (Cost et al. and Bates and Falkingham) got similar results. Choice A captures this contrast. Choice D is tempting, but a difference between two studies using the same method doesn't show that the method matters, and the two estimates actually overlap heavily.

The two condors hatched from eggs laid by females in the enclosure, but no male there could be their father. The logical conclusion is that their mothers produced them without mating, through parthenogenesis. Choice A is about the mothers' own birth, and B and D make claims about the wild or about access to males that the study didn't test.
The table shows James K. Polk with 170 total electoral college votes. The other numbers don't match Polk's electoral votes: Henry Clay received 105, and 62,103 is Birney's popular vote.

The claim is about experienced riders who mainly bike to work choosing faster routes. In choice C the rider bikes to work every day and picks the main-road bike lane over a pleasant park path 'because it's faster.' Choice D mentions biking to work but says nothing about route choice.

Saying the reader's 'true soul and body appear before me' shows the speaker claiming to see and understand the reader completely. Choice B is about making the reader his poem, and C expresses regret about not reaching the reader sooner; neither shows deep understanding.

The only difference between the two groups of plants was ELF3: plants with their own ELF3 flowered earlier at 27°C, while plants with the stiff brome version did not. This suggests ELF3 is what lets A. thaliana respond to higher temperatures. Choice B goes too far, because the study swapped the protein rather than measuring how much of it the plant produces, and A ignores that other species weren't tested.

The text lists the heliograph's weaknesses: it worked mainly in daylight and its range depended on air clarity and line of sight — all environmental conditions. So it would logically be replaced by technology less limited by those conditions. The other choices name drawbacks (cost, limited uses, Morse code) that the text never identifies.

The text explains that a portable X-ray tool let researchers analyze the shipwreck bowls without damaging them and match them to the Chinese kilns that likely made them. Choice C sums this up. Choice B reverses the logic — the kiln sites were already known, and the bowls were matched to them.

Historians of capitalism rely on archival economic records, which don't exist for much of precolonial Africa, yet Africanist scholars still found evidence of capitalism there. So the Africanists must be using other kinds of evidence. Choice B is wrong because such archival data largely doesn't exist, and nothing suggests the groups disagree about what counts as capitalism (C).

The text explains that A Clockwork Orange used mostly Beethoven arrangements and that Carlos's music for The Shining was mostly unused, leading to the conclusion that Tron has the most of her original music. Choice B contradicts the text, and D is a broad statement the text doesn't focus on.

The Chang'e 5 samples are about 2.0 billion years old, much younger than any Apollo samples (3.3 to 3.8 billion years). Choice B is false because the landing sites differ, and C is false because Apollo 17's samples (3.8) are the farthest in age from Chang'e 5's.

In choice C Electra says 'I know my own passion' (she is aware of how intense her grief is) and that because 'the causes are so dire' she will not hold back her laments (she believes the grief is justified). Choices A and D show the intensity of her grief but not her awareness or justification of it.

The text says Brâncuşi heavily influenced two major art movements but produced relatively few pieces because of his exacting standards. The disparity is between his great importance and his small output. Choice B is wrong because the text says he kept returning to the same few themes, so his work wasn't especially diverse.

A newspaper article from before August 1892 describes students reciting the pledge, which means Bellamy may not have written it. So who first wrote the pledge is now uncertain. The text doesn't discuss later changes, the newspaper's name, or students' favorite parts.

The meng- example shows a new form starting on social media and then spreading into spoken language, and similar cases occur in other languages. This suggests social media doesn't just record language change but helps cause it. Choice B is wrong because the many similar examples in other languages show the effect isn't unique to Bahasa Indonesia.

N. pudica grows on dry ridges where few plants and animals live on the surface, so traps above ground would catch little. Underground traps likely evolved to reach more prey. Choice B brings in moisture absorption, but pitchers are described as traps for prey, and nothing suggests animals bury the plant (C).

To show an overall decline since 2010, compare the start and end of the period: about 1,000 articles in 2010 versus about 500 in 2019. Choice D shows an increase from 2010 to 2013, and B wrongly calls 1,600 (the peak) the smallest number.

The narwhals behaved almost the same with ship sounds alone as with ship sounds plus sonic pulses. That would make sense if ship noise already dominated the sound environment, so adding pulses changed little. Choice C contradicts the finding of negligible differences, and D conflicts with the significant drop in deep dives under both conditions.

Delaying the middle ring's formation caused oversized super-Earths to grow from the innermost ring, which is where Earth formed. So the timing of the middle ring's formation likely helped determine how big Earth became. Choice A goes beyond the simulation results, and C talks about the outermost ring, which wasn't changed in the simulation.

The conclusion is that turmeric and South Asian-style grinding slabs at Óc Eo prove a trade link. If many South Asian people migrated to Southeast Asia, they could have brought the spice and the tool style themselves, giving an explanation that doesn't require trade. Choice D actually supports an indirect trade link through Malaysia, and C suggests broader contact rather than weakening it.

The claim is that Tobar uses journalism techniques to write fiction. Choice A shows him writing a novel by interviewing people and researching like a reporter. Choice C is the reverse — fiction techniques in nonfiction articles — and B only describes his career path.
April had 1,803 thousand housing starts, the highest of the four months. February (1,771) is the second highest, so it's the most tempting wrong choice.

The speaker wishes she could remember the first time she met the person, but the moment 'slip[ped] away' because she was 'blind... to foresee' how the relationship would grow. This expresses regret at not recalling a beginning she didn't know would matter. The poem doesn't mention an anniversary (C) or a neglected relationship (D), and its tone is regretful rather than celebratory (A).

Shared words across both branches come from the original single language, but maize words are not shared. That suggests the language had already split into northern and southern branches before the tribes acquired maize, so each branch made up its own maize vocabulary. Choice A would predict shared maize words, which is the opposite of what's found.

For participants scoring 1 through 5, the admirable-trait line is above the ignoble-trait line, but at 6 the two lines meet and at 7 ignoble-trait candidates are rated higher. That shows the usual ranking holds except for highly ignoble participants. Choice C is true but says nothing about the ignoble-trait candidates, and A is wrong because admirable-trait ratings stay nearly flat.
